newsitem.title: USA: American General to take $350 mln Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: American General to take $350 mln Q2 charge.

text.p: American General Corp said Thursday it will take a second-quarter after-tax charge of about $350 million in connection with several strategic initiatives.
The charge includes $193 million of previously disclosed charges and the settlement of certain litigation against a subsidiary, American General said.
The company, which completed its $1.8 billion acquisition of USLIFE in June, said it plans to divest certain non-strategic assets.
The company said it completed negotiations in the second quarter for the sale of its land development business to Westbrook Real Estate Fund II LP, a New York-based real estate investment operation.
American General declined to discuss the terms of the agreement.

It said these assets include master-planned residential communities in Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Texas and California and had an aggregate book value of $349 million as of May 31, 1997.
The transaction is expected to be completed in the third quarter.
In addition, the company is engaged in a process for the sale of its small Canadian life insurance subsidiary. It said the unit lacks synergy with its other life insurance operations.

As previously announced, American General's consumer finance operation sold receivables consisting of satellite dish loans, bank credit card loans and certain revolving credit home improvement loans with an aggregate book value of $752 million as of May 31, 1997.

In connection with the disposition of non-strategic assets, the company will take an after-tax charge of about $70 million in the second quarter, which includes the previously announced $26 million charge on the sale of the bank credit card loan portfolio.
The aggregate after-tax charge relating to the company's integration of USLIFE will be about $250 million, which includes the $167 million of previously disclosed acquisition-related expenses.

"These initiatives will enable American General to take advantage of our greatly expanded marketing and distribution network, build a platform for future acquisitions, and achieve significant operating efficiences in our life insurance operation," American General Chief Executive Robert Devlin said in a statement.
American General said it will record an after-tax charge of $30 million in the second quarter to resolve litigation brought against a real estate subsidiary by Avia Development Group.
The case was on appeal from a judgment of $176 million in actual and punitive damages, plus additional post-judgment interest, entered by a state district court in 1993.
